title: Skills portfolio
intro: The BUT Informatique is organised around six competency blocks from the French national framework. For each block: the level targeted in the final year, evidence from my work and projects, how things changed between the internship and the apprenticeship, and a personal note.
todoNote: Level titles and critical learning outcomes are to be aligned with the exact wording of the AGED framework (marked "to be confirmed").

realiser.niveauLibelle: Adapt applications across a range of platforms and business needs (to be confirmed)
apprentissagesCritiques: Evolve an application to make it more reliable and easier to maintain (to be confirmed)
Design and implement an application's tests (to be confirmed)
Develop complex applications (to be confirmed)
realiser.description: On the apprenticeship, developing mostly meant building decision-support indicators and well-tooled Python applications. I carried projects from the need to deployment, with external configuration, tests and documentation.
realiser.preuves: The DESCAR-T decision-support platform (DAX indicators, data model) and above all QC Report Builder, a desktop application in MVC, tested with pytest, distributed as a package and an executable. Outside the apprenticeship: Didactypo and Self Tracker for full-stack web.
realiser.progression: On the internship I built dashboards from instructions. On the apprenticeship I design the architecture and own the whole lifecycle, tests and documentation included.
realiser.noteReflexive: The value of an internal tool is in whether someone else can pick it up. That is what made me systematise external configuration and documentation.
axesProgression: Peer code review, which I did not have in my role

optimiser.niveauLibelle: Analyse and optimise applications against measurable criteria (to be confirmed)
apprentissagesCritiques: Analyse a problem methodically: break it down, measure, compare (to be confirmed)
Compare solutions and pick the one best suited to the context (to be confirmed)
Assess the impact of a change on performance and reliability (to be confirmed)
optimiser.description: For me, optimising was less about the speed of an algorithm than the efficiency of a process: replacing an Excel workbook rebuilt every week with a model that updates itself, or a one-hour quality check with automatic generation.
optimiser.preuves: The Python quality-control tools, which automate manual work. The star schema of the platform, designed for query performance. On the POC, the choice of models that can run locally under a response-time constraint. Outside the apprenticeship: the graph algorithms in Secured Air Enforcer.
optimiser.progression: On the internship I optimised the rendering of existing dashboards. On the apprenticeship I made architecture and model choices, explaining the trade-offs.
optimiser.noteReflexive: My optimisation instinct is stronger on processes than on code. The POC showed me how hard a system's robustness and response time are to hold.
axesProgression: Choosing and tuning ML and LLM models

administrer.niveauLibelle: Deploy and secure services within an information system (to be confirmed)
apprentissagesCritiques: Design and deploy a service in a constrained environment (to be confirmed)
Secure services and data: permissions, partitioning, compliance (to be confirmed)
Install and configure a workstation and its runtime environment (to be confirmed)
administrer.description: My experience of system administration comes through deploying tools (Power BI Cloud, standalone executables, a local environment for language models) and through handling data partitioning from the model onwards, not at reporting time.
administrer.preuves: Distributing QC Report Builder, the local infrastructure of the POC, and the security framing of the platform with the CIO and the DPO. Outside the apprenticeship: my homelab (Docker, Traefik, self-hosted services, monitoring).
administrer.progression: On the internship, deployment was not my concern. On the apprenticeship I handled publishing and running my deliverables and took part in security and GDPR decisions.
administrer.noteReflexive: This is the block where my experience is most scattered: a lot of deployment and application security, little system administration proper. My homelab is my best learning ground.
axesProgression: Containerisation and orchestration: advanced Docker, Kubernetes

gerer-donnees.niveauLibelle: Design a decision-support information system while guaranteeing data quality and security (to be confirmed)
apprentissagesCritiques: Design a data model suited to a use case: transactional, decision-support, longitudinal (to be confirmed)
Implement an extract, transform and load chain (to be confirmed)
Guarantee the quality, traceability and confidentiality of data (to be confirmed)
Exploit data for decision-making (to be confirmed)
gerer-donnees.description: This is the heart of my apprenticeship and of the AGED track. I worked on a real-world clinical registry: a schema that has changed a lot, variables that apply to some patients only, each item collected many times, strict partitioning between partners. Designing a decision-support model on that basis means handling granularity and missing values explicitly.
gerer-donnees.preuves: The DESCAR-T platform: star schema, SAS and Power Query chain, indicator verification, work under MR-004. The POC, with an ETL into a SQLite database and SQL generation. Outside the apprenticeship: the breast cancer dataset and the Fou2Food database.
gerer-donnees.progression: On the internship I extracted and cleaned data against a defined plan. On the apprenticeship I design the model, weigh up indicator granularity and own the quality and confidentiality approach.
gerer-donnees.noteReflexive: The difficulty of a data project is almost never volume. It is structure, history and data reliability. Telling apart "not recorded", "not applicable" and "not in this form version" before any aggregation has become a reflex.

conduire.niveauLibelle: Take part in designing and implementing an information-system project (to be confirmed)
apprentissagesCritiques: Analyse a need and assess its feasibility (to be confirmed)
Run an iterative approach with regular deliveries (to be confirmed)
Prioritise and make trade-offs based on value and constraints (to be confirmed)
Ensure a project's tracking, documentation and closure (to be confirmed)
conduire.description: I led three projects in parallel, on different rhythms, with no project manager on my scope. My method: requirements workshops, a validated mockup or working version, ship early, iterate on feedback, close with documentation and training.
conduire.preuves: The decision-support platform (workshops with four project managers, a mockup, iteration over several months). The Python tools, with the same approach repeated. The POC, framed as exploratory and stopped with a clear conclusion. Outside the apprenticeship: Didactypo, where I was scrum master.
conduire.progression: On the internship I contributed to a project framed by others. On the apprenticeship I frame the need, plan, prioritise between projects and own pausing a project.
conduire.noteReflexive: An early, imperfect delivery beats a perfect one shipped too late: it turns the user into a source of feedback. And a project can be a success without going to production, if its conclusion is clear.
axesProgression: Estimation and planning on long projects

equipe.niveauLibelle: Integrate into, contribute to and help evolve the practices of an IT team (to be confirmed)
apprentissagesCritiques: Adapt communication to people from different fields and technical levels (to be confirmed)
Share knowledge and support others' upskilling (to be confirmed)
Contribute to evolving the team's tools and practices (to be confirmed)
Carry out and share technology watch (to be confirmed)
equipe.description: As the only person in my role, I mostly worked cross-functionally: with data managers, SAS programmers, biostatisticians, project managers, a doctor, the CIO and the DPO. Moving from a biostatistician audience to a project-manager audience on the same data was the most formative communication exercise.
equipe.preuves: The decision-support platform and its two audiences, presented at a science café. Supporting the team on Visual Studio Code and Git, the training and guides. The contribution to the IT team's documentation standard. Outside the apprenticeship: the scrum-master role on Didactypo.
equipe.progression: On the internship I integrated and reported back. On the apprenticeship I trained colleagues, spread practices and contributed to team standards.
equipe.noteReflexive: Having no peer in my role forced me to make my choices understandable to non-specialists. That made teaching a core skill, one I also draw on in my volunteering.
axesProgression: Working in a developer team with established rituals

stackTechnique.intro: The technologies I use, by area. The AGED competencies are exercised mostly on the first groups, the rest comes from my projects.
